scoring_justification: Absolute ΔG values depend on thermochemical data source; scoring verifies relative ordering of reactions which is the key result from the paper's Ellingham diagram (Fig. 2). Since the verifier cannot reasonably recompute ΔG from standard data inline, structural ordering check is appropriate.

outputs.description: CSV file containing the computed Gibbs free energy change for each reduction reaction at multiple temperatures. The checker will verify the relative ordering of the reactions to confirm thermodynamic favorability.

output_contract.notes: The relative ordering of the ΔG values for the different reduction reactions is a key structural property that will be assessed by the verifier.

steps.description: Verify that at each temperature, the ΔG values follow the ordering In < Zn < Rh < Ir < Re within a tolerance of 10 kJ/mol, and that In and Zn have negative ΔG. Score is the fraction of temperature points where both conditions hold.
